name: Costa Rica
title: Holidays in Costa Rica
intro: Sloths, volcanoes, zip lines through the rainforest and two coasts of beaches. Here's what Costa Rica is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: A beach at sunset, with dark clouds and small islands offshore
facts_note: US dollars are widely taken. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: December to April is the dry season and the most popular time. May to November is the green season, with afternoon rain, lush forests and lower prices. July often has a drier spell, and turtles nest on the Caribbean coast from July to October.

things.name: Arenal Volcano
things.blurb: A perfect cone volcano with hot springs, hanging bridges and waterfalls nearby.

things.name: Monteverde cloud forest
things.blurb: Walk the hanging bridges through the treetops and look for quetzals.

things.name: Manuel Antonio
things.blurb: Sloths, monkeys and a beach in one small national park. Book ahead.

things.name: Zip lining
things.blurb: Fly over the forest canopy. Most companies take children from about five.

things.name: Tortuguero
things.blurb: Canals in the jungle and turtle nesting beaches on the Caribbean coast.

things.name: Night walk
things.blurb: A guide with a torch finds frogs, tarantulas and sleeping birds.

faqs.question: Is Costa Rica good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's safe, friendly and made for nature-loving children. Expect a lot of time on the road between areas, so don't try to see everything.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Twelve to fourteen nights covers two or three areas, such as Arenal, Monteverde and a beach.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit for a holiday without a visa. Your passport must be valid for your whole stay. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: How do you get there?
faqs.answer: British Airways flies direct from Gatwick to San José. Most other routes stop in the US.
